Introduction and meaning
Giving false evidence (old 191) — the definition of perjury. Punishment is s. 229. BNS restatement of IPC 191. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 227 is the rule on “Giving false evidence”. The section provides that whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 227 exists so that “Giving false evidence” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

The provision in detail
227. Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, in support of a just claim which B has against Z for one thousand rupees, falsely swears on a trial that he heard Z admit the justice of B’s claim. A has given false evidence

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 227 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). A, being bound by an oath to state the truth, states that he believes a certain signature to be the handwriting of Z, when he does not believe it to be the handwriting of Z. Here A states that which he knows to be false, and therefore gives false evidence

Exam use: quote illustration (b), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 227 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (c). A, knowing the general character of Z’s handwriting, states that he believes a certain signature to be the handwriting of Z; A in good faith believing it to be so. Here A’s statement is merely as to his belief, and is true as to his belief, and therefore, although the signature may not be the handwriting of Z, A has not given false evidence

Exam use: quote illustration (c), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 227 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (d). A, being bound by an oath to state the truth, states that he knows that Z was at a particular place on a particular day, not knowing anything upon the subject. A gives false evidence whether Z was at that place on the day named or not

Exam use: quote illustration (d), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 227 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (e). A, an interpreter or translator, gives or certifies as a true interpretation or translation of a statement or document which he is bound by oath to interpret or translate truly, that which is not and which he does not believe to be a true interpretation or translation. A has given false evidence

Exam use: quote illustration (e), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 227 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Explanations
Explanation 1.—A statement is within the meaning of this section, whether it is made verbally or otherwise

Explanation 2.—A false statement as to the belief of the person attesting is within the meaning of this section, and a person may be guilty of giving false evidence by stating that he believes a thing which he does not believe, as well as by stating that he knows a thing which he does not know

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 227 (Giving false evidence), Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 227 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

enhancement.definition: BNS s. 227 governs Giving false evidence. It provides: Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Safeguards judicial integrity and the administration of justice by criminalizing perjury and false statements made under legal obligation of truth.
statutoryFramework: Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences against Public Justice, BNS s. 227.

Core Legal Mandate: Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and whic...
Classification and Sentencing: Structured under Chapter XIV penal tiers.
Evidentiary and Procedural Cognate: Governed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
essentialIngredients: The commission of an act or omission falling within the statutory description of Giving false evidence.
The existence of the requisite culpable mental state (intention, knowledge, rashness, or negligence) prescribed under Section 227.
The absence of any statutory justification, exception, or lawful authority under Chapter III (General Exceptions).
The resulting consequence or endangerment specified in the statutory formula of Section 227.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 227 defines perjury (giving false evidence). It requires: (1) a person legally bound by oath, affirmation, or express provision of law to state the truth; (2) making any statement which is false; and (3) knowing or believing it to be false, or not believing it to be true. The section applies to judicial proceedings, police statements recorded under legal obligation, affidavits, and statutory declarations. The statement can be verbal or in writing, and covers electronic affidavits.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of giving false evidence under Section 227 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 227.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 227 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Giving false evidence (s. 227) vs Fabricating false evidence (s. 228): Section 227 involves false spoken/written testimony by a witness; Section 228 involves creating artificial circumstantial evidence or false entries.
Section 227 vs Section 217 (False information to public servant): Section 227 requires an oath or express legal obligation of truth; Section 217 covers general administrative information.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 227 for conduct relating to giving false evidence.
Rule: Under BNS s. 227, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 227.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 227 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
